input.question: Can someone explain what a mortgage is (LI5)?
input.ground_truth: A mortgage is simply a loan that a bank gives you so that you can buy a house. Most people don't have enough money on hand to pay the full price for a house so they will get a loan from the bank, called a mortgage, that is to be used strictly for the purchase of a house. The bank requires you to pay back a certain amount of the loan, with interest, every month just like any other loan. If you stop paying your mortgage the bank has the legal right to foreclose on your home, which means that they can force you to leave and sell the house to get their money back. Once you pay back your mortgage in full the bank no longer has any legal claim on your house.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you want a big toy, but you don't have enough money to buy it right now. So, you ask your parents if you can pay for it little by little over time. Your parents say, "Yes, but we will keep the toy until you finish paying for it." That's kind of like a mortgage.

A mortgage is when you want to buy a really big thing, like a house, but you don't have all the money at once. So, you promise to pay a little bit of money every month for many years. While you are paying, the bank (or someone else) keeps the "key" to the house, but you get to live there. Once you finish paying all the money, the house is all yours!
